high.title: Dollar-Won Takes Breather on Softer PCE, Closes at 1,543.10 Won
high.summary: The USD/KRW exchange rate closed at 1,543.10 in overnight New York trading, rising only modestly by 1.30 won from the prior Seoul session close. The limited upside came despite a brief dollar index pullback — its first correction in four sessions — triggered by softer-than-expected U.S. PCE inflation data. Two key forces contained the dollar's gains against the won: (1) the dollar index itself retreating on the benign PCE print, and (2) exporter-driven KRW supply pressure intensifying ahead of month-end and half-year-end settlements, a recurring seasonal dynamic that typically sees Korean exporters converting dollar receivables into won.

high.title: US Core PCE Price Index Rises 0.3% MoM in May, Maintaining Moderate Pace
high.summary:
The US core PCE price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.3% month-on-month in May, in line with market expectations and maintaining a moderate trajectory. Headline PCE came in at 0.4% MoM. The fact that core inflation neither surprised to the upside nor downside is meaningful for KRW/USD dynamics: a benign reading reduces the probability of additional Fed tightening, which in turn alleviates upward pressure on the USD and provides some relief for the Korean Won. For BOK watchers, a contained US inflation print gives the Fed less urgency to hold rates higher for longer, potentially narrowing the Korea-US rate differential concern that has weighed on KRW. Bond investors should note that this reading supports a stable or modestly lower US Treasury yield environment near-term, which could provide a tailwind for Korean government bonds. Watch for follow-through in upcoming US labor market data and any Fed communications that could shift the rate differential calculus, as this remains the dominant macro driver for KRW and foreign capital flows into Korean fixed income.

high.title: Foreign Buying Drives Bond Rally; 3-Year KTB Yield Falls 3.5bp Amid Equity Sell-Off and Suspected FX Intervention
high.summary: South Korean government bond yields fell sharply on June 26th, with short- to medium-term maturities leading the rally. The move was driven by a classic risk-off rotation as domestic equities underwent a sharp correction, pushing investors into the relative safety of KTBs. Foreign investors were notable buyers, adding an important cross-border capital flow dimension to the rally. The session's most significant development was a late-session plunge in the dollar-won exchange rate, which market participants attributed to suspected official intervention by Korean authorities — a key signal for FX traders monitoring BOK tolerance levels for KRW strength. Ultra-long bond yields bucked the trend, edging higher on auction supply concerns, creating a notable flattening/inversion dynamic at the long end. **Key implications:** Foreign bond inflows are supportive of KRW and suggest continued appetite for Korean duration. Suspected intervention signals that authorities may be capping the pace of won appreciation. Watch for follow-through foreign buying and any official BOK commentary confirming intervention activity.

high.title: IRS Rates Plunge in Short-to-Medium Maturities on Equity Correction and Won Strength
high.summary: Interest rate swap (IRS) rates fell sharply across the curve on June 26th, with the 1-year rate declining 3.75bp to 3.4550%, the 3-year falling 5.50bp, and the 5-year down 5.25bp. The magnitude of the move — particularly concentrated in the 3-to-5 year belly — reflects aggressive safe-haven buying as equity markets corrected. The concurrent strengthening of the Korean won reinforced bullish fixed income sentiment, as a firmer KRW reduces imported inflation pressure and bolsters rate-cut expectations. **Key implications for bond and rates traders:** The steepness of the IRS move relative to the cash KTB market (see Article 3) suggests strong receive-side interest in the swap market, potentially from domestic institutions hedging equity exposure. The 3–5 year sector appears to be the market's preferred expression of a BOK easing view. Monitor whether IRS rates stabilize or extend declines if equity weakness persists into the next session.

high.title: [FX Close] Won Plunges 10.70 Won on Suspected Authorities' Intervention
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate fell sharply by 10.70 won to close at 1,532.00 won as of 3:30 p.m. KST in the Seoul foreign exchange market — marking the first decline in five consecutive trading sessions. The move was notably dramatic given that the session opened at 1,547.30 won, up 4.60 won from the prior day, suggesting initial upward pressure on USD/KRW before authorities stepped in. The reversal is widely attributed to suspected FX intervention by Korean monetary authorities, who appear to have deployed significant dollar-selling flows to cap the won's weakness.

medium.title: Chicago Fed President: 'Inflation Moving in Wrong Direction... Slight Improvement in Services Sector'
medium.summary: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee expressed concern on June 25 that U.S. inflation "has recently been moving in the wrong direction," noting the Fed has been above its 2% target for five consecutive years. He flagged the services sector as particularly worrying, though he noted some marginal improvement there. Goolsbee's cautious tone signals that the Fed is in no hurry to cut rates, reinforcing a higher-for-longer U.S. rate environment. For KRW and Korean bond investors, a delayed Fed easing cycle sustains upward pressure on USD/KRW and limits the BOK's room to cut rates aggressively without risking capital outflows. Watch subsequent Fed speakers and the next CPI/PCE prints for directional cues on U.S. monetary policy divergence with the BOK.

medium.title: US 7-Year Treasury Auction Draws Solid Demand, Yield Meets Expectations
medium.summary: The U.S. Treasury successfully auctioned $44 billion in 7-year notes at a yield of 4.260%, down 3 basis points from last month's 4.290%, suggesting moderate easing in the belly of the U.S. yield curve. The bid-to-cover ratio slipped marginally to 2.50x from 2.52x but remained slightly above the recent average, indicating healthy underlying demand from both domestic and foreign buyers. For Korean government bond (KTB) markets, well-absorbed U.S. Treasury supply reduces the risk of a disorderly global rates selloff that could spill over into emerging market bonds. Stable U.S. 7-year yields near 4.26% continue to create a significant rate differential versus KTBs, which remains a structural headwind for foreign capital inflows into Korean fixed income. Monitor the long-end of the U.S. curve for any signs of demand fatigue that could pressure KTB yields higher.

medium.title: US and Gulf States Affirm Hormuz Strait Freedom of Navigation as 'Essential for Regional and Global Security'
medium.summary: The United States and all six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states issued a joint statement on June 25 emphasizing that unrestricted freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz is essential for both regional and global security, in direct opposition to Iran's threat to close the waterway. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical chokepoint for global oil supply, and any disruption would have outsized implications for Korea, which is heavily dependent on Middle Eastern energy imports. An escalation in Hormuz tensions would likely push crude oil prices sharply higher, worsening Korea's trade balance and current account, exerting depreciation pressure on the KRW, and adding imported inflation that complicates BOK rate policy. The unified U.S.-GCC statement is a near-term stabilizing signal, but the situation warrants close monitoring given its direct macro relevance for Korea's external accounts and FX dynamics.

medium.title: Audit Agency to Probe Regulators Over Leveraged ETF Boom
medium.summary:
South Korea's Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) has launched a comprehensive audit of the Financial Services Commission (FSC) and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) in response to rising investor risks following recent market volatility. The probe focuses on the rapid mainstreaming of leveraged ETFs and other high-risk products, with concerns centring on excessive costs and potential mis-selling to retail investors. While not a direct FX or rates event, this regulatory action signals heightened scrutiny of Korean financial market supervision at a sensitive time — coming just two days after what markets dubbed "Black Tuesday" on June 23rd. For international fund managers, increased regulatory oversight of derivative and leveraged products could affect market liquidity and retail participation dynamics, which in turn influence KOSPI volatility and indirectly, foreign investor sentiment toward Korean capital markets.

medium.title: KOSPI Surges 5.42% to Close at 8,930 — SK Hynix Soars 13%
medium.summary: While individual equity performance typically falls outside our core coverage, a single-day KOSPI surge of 5.42% to 8,930 is a macro-relevant event that warrants monitoring. Moves of this magnitude can signal significant shifts in foreign investor risk appetite toward Korean assets, with potential knock-on effects for KRW demand and short-term capital flow dynamics. SK Hynix's 13% gain suggests a tech/semiconductor-led rally, possibly driven by global AI sentiment or positive demand signals. Fund managers with cross-asset Korea exposure should note that sharp equity rallies of this scale can attract foreign portfolio inflows, providing temporary KRW support. Conversely, if the rally is driven by domestic retail momentum rather than foreign buying, the FX impact may be muted. Content was truncated in the feed — full details on volume, foreign net buying/selling, and index drivers should be verified via Bloomberg or KRX data before drawing firm FX or flow conclusions.

medium.title: President Lee Signals Supplementary Budget for GPU Procurement
medium.summary: President Lee Jae-myung has flagged the possibility of a supplementary budget (추경) to accelerate domestic GPU procurement as part of Korea's national AI infrastructure strategy, discussed at a Blue House strategy meeting on June 26. While the primary driver is AI/tech policy, a supplementary budget has direct fiscal implications worth monitoring: additional government bond issuance to fund the extra budget could pressure Korean Treasury bond (KTB) yields higher by increasing supply in the market. If the supplementary budget is sizable, it may also raise near-term fiscal deficit concerns, adding a mild bearish tone to the KTB market. Bond traders should watch for official budget size announcements from the Ministry of Economy and Finance, as well as any National Assembly approval timeline. A second, shorter article on the same topic (Article 5) is duplicative and has been consolidated here.

medium.title: FX Swap Points Rise on Month-End Won Demand
medium.summary: FX swap points rose across all tenors on June 26th, driven by month-end Korean won funding demand. The 1-year swap point closed at -14.90 won (up 0.30 won), the 6-month at -6.80 won (up 0.20 won), and the 3-month at -2.80 won (up 0.15 won). The rise in swap points reflects tighter short-term won liquidity at month-end, a recurring seasonal pattern. For FX and cross-currency basis traders, the narrowing of deeply negative swap points signals reduced won funding stress in the near term, which is mildly supportive of KRW. Combined with the suspected official FX intervention noted in Article 3, month-end positioning dynamics are adding a technical layer to KRW movement today. Watch for swap point normalization post-month-end as a gauge of underlying dollar-won liquidity conditions.

medium.title: Top 5 Banks' Loan-Deposit Rate Spread Holds Steady at 1.392%
medium.summary: The average loan-deposit rate spread for household loans at Korea's five major banks (KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Hana, Woori, NH Nonghyup) stood at 1.392 percentage points in the latest month, up just 0.004 percentage points from the prior month — effectively flat. The stability of this spread suggests that competitive pressures and regulatory oversight on bank lending margins remain intact, with neither a material widening (which would indicate banks pricing in more risk) nor a compression (which could signal aggressive lending competition). For bond investors, a stable NIM environment suggests no immediate stress in the banking sector's funding dynamics, which is broadly neutral for Korean financial credit spreads. This metric will become more relevant if the BOK proceeds with rate cuts, as further easing could pressure deposit rates faster than lending rates, potentially squeezing margins.

medium.title: Meritz Securities Issues 368 Billion Won Private Subordinated Bonds at 5.6%
medium.summary:
Meritz Securities issued 368 billion won (~$310 million) in private subordinated bonds on June 26, priced at a coupon rate of 5.60% per annum with a 30-year maturity. The bonds include a rate reset mechanism every five years, with the revised rate calculated as the base rate plus a spread, plus an additional 200 basis points premium. Meritz Fire & Marine Insurance provided 70 billion won in support for the issuance. The 5.60% pricing on a subordinated financial sector instrument provides a useful reference data point for Korean credit spreads and investor appetite for longer-duration, lower-rated paper. The willingness of institutional investors to absorb this issuance at current rate levels suggests the domestic bond market retains reasonable depth, though the subordinated and private placement structure limits broader market read-through.
